recipes.name: Sausage Crescent Rolls
ingredients_raw: 1 pound fresh, ground spicy pork sausage

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a medium skillet, lightly brown sausage and drain. While sausage is still hot, add cream cheese and stir until cheese is melted and mixture is creamy. Cool completely.

Separate crescent rolls and arrange into two rectangles. Form log of sausage mixture lengthwise down center of each rectangle. Fold over the long sides of pastry to cover sausage log. Place on ungreased cookie sheet, seam down. Brush with egg white and sprinkle with poppy seeds.
Bake 20 minutes until crust is golden. When completely cooled, slice into one and one-half inch slices.

raw_recipe.headline: Sausage Crescent Rolls
raw_recipe.description: Spicy seasoned sausage mixed with cream cheese and wrapped in crescent rolls. For a different variation, add thin slices of pepperoni on the bottom of crescent roll before the sausage mixture and shred cheddar on top of sausage; roll pastry over.

review.reviewBody: Very good! Instead of making as directed, I cut small squares from the crescent dough and made cups in a small muffin tin. I then put filling in and baked them. Nice individual appetizers and my boys loved them!

My family has made a different version of this for years and still loves it adults and kids and coworkers and friends. Take 1 lb sausage, cook (I micro for 5 min, drain) add 1 block cream cheese (micro for 1 min to soften). Stir together. Put 1 whole can cresent rolls in bottom of greased 13x9 pan, pinch seams. Put all mix on top. Add second can of cresent rolls pinch seams and sides. Bake for time on roll can. May need extra 3-4 min. Much faster and easier than individual triangles.

My go to football dish to pass recipe!!! Using mini muffin pans with bits of croissant dough. Only use the Jimmy Dean or Bob Evans' hot/spicy, cream cheese, and red pepper flakes. that's it, and these get demolished!!!! when I'm hosting, I can't serve them fast enough!!!

I made a mistake and bought plain ground turkey instead of turkey sausage, so I added some garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper and sage when browning the turkey. I also finely diced one medium onion and sauteed it along with the turkey. After adding the onion (which was an excellent addition) and the cream cheese, I found that the mixture was a bit too thick so I just poured in about 1/8 or 1/4 cup milk which made it perfect. It was easier for me to lay out half the crescent dough onto the cookie sheet, put the meat mixture in the middle of it in the shape of a log, and then place the other unrolled half of the dough on top of it and close all the seams. I didn't have poppy seeds but these turned out golden and delicious! My husband liked them too. Even though they were great with plain ground turkey, next time I will definitely try turkey sausage. I think it will be even better.

I am generally not much of a fan of crescent rolls but these were really good. I used bulk mild Italian sausage, 1/4 cup diced onions plus all of the other ingredients. It made 8 sausage crescent rolls. when I used a pair of triangle of dough for each roll. I sauteed the onion along with the sausage. I made individual sausage crescent rolls and I did use the egg white but not the poppy seeds. I ate one one of the rolls while it was hot and fresh with some fluffy scrambled eggs and froze the rest of the sausage crescent rolls for a quick to reheat breakfast during the week. Andy, thanks for this quick to make and tasty recipe!

After reading the reviews, I used the muffin tin idea. I used one chub turkey sausage and one chub of vegetarain sausage-cooked in separate pans. So, one package of cresent rolls for each kind of meat. Two trays of tins to keep them seperate. Lastly, I reduced the cream cheese by half and used garlic & herb. Served the sausage puffs with a green salad & butternut squash soup...delicious!

I just finished making these for a memorial service tomorrow...I did tweet with the recipe...i added one envelope of Ranch dressing mix to two pounds of sausage and added onion powder and garlic powder...I made a 4 lb sausage batch...my little logs must have been bigger than others as I only used 7 cans of crescent rolls..I let them cool off in refrigerator to cool before slicing...when I sliced them I just cut each one in 1/4ths which is a little bigger than 1 1/2 inches...the recipe calls for ungreased cookie sheet but found they turned out better with a little non-stick spray on bottom of cookie sheet worked better...and would make up six at a time to place on cookie sheet...with so many made I place tooth picks in after I sliced them...everybody loves them...I served them cold..

I have been preparing this for years, but as written it is quite bland. Here are my modifications: brown the sausage with half a diced onion and garlic. Add a dash of cayenne pepper. Substitute Velveeta for the cream cheese...cube up a two inch chunk and mix in while sausage is still hot. I have also tried some shredded carrot and bell pepper. Makes a very pretty presentation. I don't bother with the poppy seed or egg wash. This is always a favorite appetizer.

This was easy and delicious! I halved this recipe and it still made a lot! I used a half lb. of Jimmy Dean plain ground sausage and added 1/4 tsp. each of crushed red pepper, black pepper and onion powder while cooking the sausage, before stirring in the half pkg. of cream cheese. Toughest part of this recipe was flipping the roll over to seam side down. Hubby loved it with his eggs for Sunday breakfast!

I make it as called out with cream cheese.
I also make one with cooking the sausage saving drippings add butter flour cook the flour down and add milk and cheddar. add garlic and cayenne pepper.

I make a similar recipe just prepared a little differently. I roll the Crescent dough flat making sure the seams are well pressed together. Spread 4 oz of softened cream cheese over the dough. Then spread the cooked sausage over the cream cheese and roll it up like a cinnamon roll. Then slice the roll with a bread (serrated) knife. I can usually get about 12-13 slices out of the roll. Lay them flat on a grease cookie sheet and cook at 350 for about 15-18 minutes. They come out as perfect sausage rolls. Mmmmm!

Yum!! Had a few cans of expiring crescent roll dough and voila, dinner is served. Added my go-to spices (SPGO), Italian seasoning and can of original Rotel (because I use it in nearly everything). Very tasty and adaptable to what you have on hand.

I really liked this, I didn't have any refrigerated crescent rolls so I used used Pepperidge Farms puff pastry. I rolled one sheet out to about 14 x 9 inched, cut in half the short way, put the filling across the center of each rectangle the long way and rolled it up. brushed them with avocado oil. Then baked at 350 for 20 -25 minutes and turned the heat up to 400 to brown the pastry.
It was gone almost as quickly as it was made! Definitely a keeper! I cut mine up like pinwheels and served them as an appetizer for Christmas.
This has become a family favorite. The spicy sausage is the secret.
Delicious and easy to make!
I made this just as it was directed. It turned out great! Thank you for sharing!
Just made this for dinner. Really good, but somewhat salty. I did add the pepperoni and a little sharp cheddar. Served with some pizza sauce. Will be making again!
This is the only recipe we have that uses hot breakfast sausage, but it's going in the weekend breakfast rotation.

This was a tasty fun breakfast meal. It looks so fancy and would impress family or guests. I didn't understand why you would cool it completely though and then cut and serve. Why would you want to eat it cool? I served mine whole and warm with some sausage gravy drizzled over the top. Yum!!!
